threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and initial backlog for the onboarding rollout.

messages.text: Welcome to the Hybrid Customer Onboarding Workspace Rollout project. We have 21 days to design and pilot a standardized onboarding process that works for both office and remote teams. This thread is for us to align on scope, success criteria, and the initial backlog. Let's start by confirming what we're building and what we're explicitly NOT building in this phase.

Good kickoff. Before we lock scope, I want to clarify the boundaries. Are we redesigning the entire customer lifecycle, or just the first 30 days post-contract? And are we including post-onboarding support handoff, or stopping at 'customer ready to work'? These affect the workflow complexity significantly.

That's a solid question. From what I understand, we're focusing on the initial onboarding phase—from contract signature through the customer's first project kickoff. Post-onboarding support and ongoing account management are separate streams. Does that align with everyone's understanding?

Yes, that makes sense. So we're not touching renewal workflows or upsell processes. Just the initial onboarding. I'd also suggest we keep the scope to internal process and templates—we're not building new tools, just standardizing how we use what we have.

Agreed. So D1 is locked: scope is initial onboarding from contract to project kickoff, internal process and templates only, no new tools. Now let's talk success metrics. What should we track to know if this rollout is working?

I think we should track cycle time—how many days from contract to customer ready. Also errors or rework cycles, and maybe adoption rate—how many teams are actually using the new templates and workspace. Those would go into A4, the KPI tracking sheet.

Cycle time is good. I'd add one more: customer satisfaction or feedback score during onboarding. We want to make sure the new process doesn't slow things down or create friction. Should we set baseline targets for the pilot?
For the pilot, I'd suggest we just capture the metrics without hard targets. We need a baseline first. Once we see the pilot results, we can set realistic targets for rollout. Agree?
Makes sense. So D2: we track cycle time, rework cycles, adoption rate, and customer feedback in A4. No hard targets for pilot, baseline only. That gives us data to inform the full rollout decision.

Perfect. D1 and D2 are confirmed. Now let's map the initial backlog. We need to start with T1—mapping the current as-is process. Who's taking that? We need interviews with at least 3 recent project owners.
I can lead T1. I've worked on several recent projects and know the team. I'll schedule interviews with the project owners and document the as-is workflow. Should have that done by end of week.
Good. Once T1 is done, T2 follows—designing the target workflow and RACI. I can pick that up and work with 95041 on the design. We'll need input from sales management and PMO for approval.
And I'll handle T3 and T7—the templates and checklists. I can draft those in parallel while you're working on the workflow. Once the workflow is locked, I'll align the checklists to the steps.
Great. So the initial backlog is: T1 (98050), T2 (119847 + 95041), T3 and T7 (14637), and we'll need T12 for the KPI sheet. 14637, can you also own T12?
Yes, I can do T12. I'll set up the KPI sheet with the metrics we agreed—cycle time, rework, adoption, and feedback. Should be ready by mid-week.

One thing to flag: T4 is the legal and compliance review of templates. That's critical path. We should send templates to legal as soon as T3 is drafted, not wait until everything is perfect. They'll need time to review.
Good catch. 14637, once you have the first draft of T3, we'll send it to legal immediately. We can't wait for perfection. They'll give us feedback and we iterate.

Alright, TH1 summary: D1 and D2 locked. Initial backlog assigned. T1 starts today (98050), T3 draft by mid-week (14637), T12 by mid-week (14637), T2 design starts after T1 (119847 + 95041). T4 legal review starts as soon as T3 draft is ready. Next sync in TH2 for workflow and workspace design.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the target onboarding workflow, RACI, and workspace structure.

messages.text: Sharing the first draft of the target onboarding workflow and RACI matrix. This is based on T1 interviews and consolidates the best practices we found. The workflow has 8 major steps from contract to kickoff. Workspace structure proposal is also attached—we're using a folder hierarchy with customer name, phase, and document type.

I've reviewed the draft. The workflow is clean, but I see a potential bottleneck at step 5—legal review of customer data. Currently it's sequential, but we could run it in parallel with step 4 if we clarify the data requirements upfront. That could save 2-3 days.

Good point. Let me check with the legal team on that. If we can parallelize, we should. I'll update the workflow and repost. On the RACI, I have sales owning steps 1-3, project team owning 4-6, and customer success owning 7-8. Does that feel right?
The RACI looks reasonable, but I'd suggest we add a 'consulted' role for IT on steps 4 and 5. They need to know about access provisioning early, not just at the end. Otherwise we'll have delays.
Absolutely. I'll add IT as consulted on steps 4-5. That's a critical dependency. Let me revise and repost by tomorrow.

On the workspace structure—A6 looks good. I like the naming convention: /Customer_Name/Phase/DocumentType. One question: how do we handle shared documents that span multiple customers, like templates or guidelines? Should those live in a separate 'Shared' folder at the root?

Yes, good catch. I'll add a /Shared folder for templates, guidelines, and reusable assets. That keeps customer workspaces clean and makes it easy to update shared docs without touching individual customer folders.

I have a question on access control. Who decides who gets access to each customer workspace? Is it the project manager, or do we need IT to provision? And what about remote staff—do they get the same access as office staff?

That's part of the workspace structure definition. I'd suggest: project manager requests access, IT provisions it. Access rules should be the same for office and remote—no difference. We document that in A6 so it's clear.

Agreed. I'll add that to A6. Now, we also need to think about T5 and T6—defining the structure and then configuring the pilot workspace. Should we do a test run of the structure with a dummy customer before we go live with the real pilot?

Yes, absolutely. We should validate the structure with a test customer first. That way we catch any naming issues, access problems, or missing folders before we run the real pilot. I can help with that validation.

Good. So here's the plan: I'll revise A1 with the parallel legal review and IT consulted role. I'll update A6 with the /Shared folder and access rules. We'll do a test run of T5 and T6 with a dummy customer. Once that's validated, we're ready for D3 and D4 approval.
119847, when can you have the revised A1 and A6 ready for approval? We need to move fast to stay on the 21-day timeline.
I'll have the revised versions by EOD tomorrow. Then we do the test run with 95041 on the dummy customer—that should take a day. So we can lock D3 and D4 by end of week.

One more thing—we should also think about A8, the IT request ticket. We need to formally request IT to set up the shared workspace infrastructure. That should go in as soon as we approve the structure.
Right. I'll draft A8 once A6 is finalized. That way IT has all the details they need. We can submit it right after D4 is locked.

Perfect. TH2 summary: A1 and A6 revisions in progress. Test run of workspace structure planned. D3 (workflow and RACI approval) and D4 (workspace structure approval) locked by end of week. A8 IT request follows. Next thread is TH3 for templates and compliance.

threads.thread_goal: Create and validate templates, checklists, and compliance aspects.

messages.text: Posting the first draft of templates and checklists. A5 has the email and document templates—welcome email, data collection form, project kickoff agenda, and handoff checklist. A3 has the internal checklists for sales, project, and customer success teams. These are aligned with the workflow steps from T2.

Good start. I've reviewed the templates. The structure is clear, but I notice the data collection form doesn't specify which fields are mandatory vs. optional. That could cause confusion. Can you add a legend or note?
Good point. I'll add a legend—red for mandatory, yellow for optional, and gray for 'nice to have'. That should make it clearer. I'll update A5 by tomorrow.
On the checklists—A3 looks good, but I'd suggest we add a 'sign-off' column. Each step should have a checkbox and a date/initials field. That way we have an audit trail.
Great idea. I'll add sign-off columns to all three checklists. That also helps with compliance tracking.
Now the critical question: have we sent these to legal and compliance yet? T4 is the legal review, and we need their sign-off before we can use these in the pilot. What's the status?

Not yet—I wanted to get feedback from the team first. But you're right, we should send to legal now. I'll send the current draft to legal today, even though we're still refining. They can start reviewing while we make updates.

Good. 14637, when you send to legal, include a note that we're still refining based on team feedback, but we need their input on data protection and compliance. Ask them to flag any issues with the data collection form and the customer-facing templates.
Will do. I'll send today with a note about the timeline and ask for feedback by end of week.

One thing I want to check—the project kickoff agenda template. Does it include time for discussing the onboarding process itself? We should make sure the customer understands what they're going through and why.
Good catch. The current template is pretty bare. I'll add a section for 'onboarding overview and next steps' so the customer knows what to expect.

Also, we need to think about T8—the quick-start guide for staff. That's A2. We should draft that in parallel with the templates. It should reference the templates and checklists and explain how to use them.
I can draft A2 once the templates and checklists are finalized. It'll be easier to write the guide when I know exactly what we're guiding people through.
Timeline check: when do you think A5 and A3 will be ready for D5 sign-off? We need to move fast.

I'll have the updated versions with the legend, sign-off columns, and kickoff agenda section by EOD tomorrow. Then legal reviews. If they come back with minor feedback, I can incorporate by end of week. So D5 sign-off by Friday.
And D6—legal and compliance confirmation. That depends on their review. 14637, make sure you follow up with legal by Wednesday if you don't hear back. We can't wait until Friday.
Understood. I'll send today and follow up Wednesday. If there are any blockers, I'll escalate immediately.

TH3 summary: A5 and A3 drafts updated by EOD tomorrow with team feedback. Legal review starts today. D5 (template sign-off) and D6 (compliance confirmation) targeted for Friday. A2 quick-start guide drafted after templates finalized. Next thread is TH4 for pilot planning.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate the pilot onboarding execution and training.

messages.text: Time to lock in the pilot customer and timeline. We need a customer that's ready to start onboarding in the next 7-10 days. Ideally, a mid-sized deal with a straightforward project scope—not too complex, but real enough to test the process. Who do we have in the pipeline?
I have a customer—TechCorp—that signed last week. They're ready to kick off in 8 days. It's a 6-month project, moderate complexity. They're a good fit for the pilot. Sales team is aligned.

Perfect. TechCorp it is. So D7: pilot customer is TechCorp, onboarding starts in 8 days. That means we need to have the workspace set up, templates finalized, and team trained by then. Can we make that timeline?

Tight, but doable. T6 is configuring the pilot workspace—we can do that in 2 days once the structure is approved. Templates should be finalized by Friday. Training is the question. How are we doing that?

Good question. T9 is the training session. We have two options: live session early next week, or recorded session that people can watch async. Given the timeline, I'm leaning toward a live session on Monday morning, then a recorded version for anyone who can't make it.
Live session makes sense. But we need to make sure everyone who's involved in the pilot attends. That's sales, project team, and customer success. Can we make it mandatory for the pilot team?
Yes, mandatory for the pilot team. We'll also record it for the broader rollout later. So D8: live training session Monday morning, mandatory for pilot team, recorded for async viewing.
I can help prepare the training materials. I'll work with 119847 to create slides and a walkthrough of the templates, checklists, and workspace. We'll need A2 finalized first, though.

Good. A2 should be ready by Friday. So we have the weekend to prep training materials, and we run the session Monday morning. That gives us Monday afternoon to address any questions before TechCorp kicks off Tuesday.
One thing—we should also brief the TechCorp customer on the new process. They should know they're part of a pilot and that we're collecting feedback. That's part of T10, the pilot execution.
I'll handle that. I'll send TechCorp a note explaining the pilot, the new process, and that we'll be asking for feedback. They're usually open to that kind of thing.

Great. So the pilot timeline: workspace configured by Friday (T6), training Monday morning (T9), TechCorp onboarding starts Tuesday (T10). We'll collect feedback throughout and document in the pilot report.
Who's owning T10—the pilot execution and feedback collection? That's critical.
I'll own T10. I'll coordinate with the pilot team daily, track progress against the workflow, and collect feedback from sales, project, and customer success. We'll also get feedback from TechCorp.
And A8—the IT request. We need to make sure IT has everything they need to set up the workspace. Is that submitted yet?
A8 was submitted after D4 was locked. IT should have it. Let me check on the status and make sure they're on track for Friday.

TH4 summary: D7 locked—TechCorp is pilot customer, starts Tuesday. D8 locked—live training Monday morning, mandatory for pilot team, recorded for async. T6 workspace config by Friday, T9 training Monday, T10 pilot execution starts Tuesday. Next thread is TH5 for pilot results and rollout decision.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results, adjust process, and agree on rollout plan.

messages.text: Pilot onboarding with TechCorp is complete. I'm sharing the pilot summary report—A7. Overall, the process worked well, but we found a few issues that need fixing before full rollout. Cycle time was 6 days, which is good. We had one rework cycle due to missing data in the customer form. Customer feedback was positive.
Good results. What were the key issues? I see the rework cycle—was that the data collection form we discussed? And what did the team feedback say?

Yes, the data collection form was one issue. The customer didn't understand which fields were mandatory, even with the legend. We need to make it clearer—maybe add examples or a note at the top. The other issue was the workspace structure—the project team found the folder naming confusing at first. They wanted a 'Current' folder to see active items.
I can fix the data collection form. I'll add a note at the top explaining mandatory vs. optional, and maybe add a sample filled-out version. That should help.

On the workspace structure—adding a 'Current' folder is a good idea. It's a simple change to A6. We can add a note that 'Current' contains active items, and archived items go to 'Completed'. That's intuitive.
Good. So D9: we're making two changes—clarify the data collection form with examples and a note, and add a 'Current' folder to the workspace structure. Both are minor and shouldn't delay rollout.
What about the KPI data? Did we capture the metrics we planned? Cycle time, rework, adoption, feedback?

Yes, all captured in A4. Cycle time: 6 days. Rework cycles: 1. Adoption: 100% of the pilot team used the new workspace and templates. Customer feedback: 4.5 out of 5 on ease of use. Those are good baselines.
Those are solid numbers. The 6-day cycle time is reasonable, and 100% adoption is great. One rework cycle is acceptable for a pilot. I think we're ready to roll out.
Agreed. But we should make the changes to A5 and A6 first, then do a quick validation before we roll out to the broader team. That's T11—consolidate learnings and update.
Right. T11 is on my list. I'll update A5 and A6 based on the pilot feedback, and we'll do a quick review. That should take 2-3 days. Then we're ready for D10—the go/no-go decision.
When can you have T11 done? We're at day 18 of the 21-day timeline. We need to move fast.

I'll have the updated A5 and A6 ready by tomorrow EOD. Quick review by 95041 and 14637 on Wednesday. D10 decision by Wednesday evening. That gives us time to brief the broader team and start rollout by day 21.
I can review Wednesday morning. But I want to make sure we're not just saying 'go' without thinking about the rollout plan. What's the timeline for rolling out to the rest of the organization?

Good point. D10 should include both the go/no-go decision AND the rollout timeline. I'm thinking: go ahead with rollout, start with the next 3 customers in the pipeline, then expand to all new customers by end of month. Does that work?
That's reasonable. Three customers gives us a chance to catch any issues before full rollout. And end of month is realistic for training the broader team.

TH5 summary: Pilot results are positive. D9 locked—minor updates to A5 and A6 based on feedback. T11 updates by tomorrow EOD. D10 decision by Wednesday—go ahead with rollout, start with 3 customers, expand to all new customers by end of month. Project is on track.
